questions.text: CSS 2025 · Pair: Blurt / Blert — Which meaning fits “Blurt”?

options.A: To refer to something indirectly, without naming it
options.B: To say something suddenly and without thinking
options.C: A short, witty saying expressing a clever idea
options.D: A foolish or stupid person (dialect slang)

questions.explanation:
Blurt: To say something suddenly and without thinking. Sentence: "Unable to keep the secret, the boy blurted out the news of the surprise party."
Blert: (British, Liverpool/Merseyside slang) a foolish or stupid person. Sentence: "Only a blert would leave his car unlocked with the keys inside in a crowded market."
Source: CSS 2025 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2025 · Pair: Defenestration / Dénouement — Which meaning fits “Defenestration”?

options.A: A long period of abnormally low rainfall causing water shortage
options.B: To cut wool or hair with large blades; to break under strain
options.C: The act of throwing someone or something out of a window
options.D: The final resolution of a story's plot

questions.explanation:
Defenestration: The act of throwing someone or something out of a window. Sentence: "The 1618 Defenestration of Prague, when officials were thrown out of a castle window, helped start the Thirty Years' War."
Dénouement: The final part of a story or play in which the plot is resolved. Sentence: "In the dénouement, the detective reveals the murderer and all mysteries are explained."
Source: CSS 2025 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2025 · Pair: Vallum / Vellum — Which meaning fits “Vallum”?

options.A: A rampart or defensive wall/earthwork, especially around a Roman camp
options.B: Utter, absolute; very steep; (of fabric) very thin
options.D: The final part of a story or play in which the plot is resolved

questions.explanation:
Vallum: A rampart or defensive wall/earthwork, especially around a Roman camp. Sentence: "The Roman soldiers built a vallum of earth and stakes around their camp for protection."
Vellum: Fine parchment made from calfskin, used for writing or binding. Sentence: "The ancient Quran manuscript was written on vellum that has lasted for centuries."
Source: CSS 2025 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2025 · Pair: Sow / Sough — Which meaning fits “Sow”?

options.B: (Adjective) relying on someone or something for support; determined by
options.C: To scatter or plant seeds; (noun) a female pig
options.D: A soft murmuring or sighing sound, as of wind

questions.explanation:
Sow: To scatter or plant seeds; (noun) a female pig. Sentence: "Farmers sow wheat in November and harvest it in April."
Sough: A soft murmuring, sighing or rustling sound, as of wind in trees; to make it. Sentence: "At night we heard only the sough of the wind through the pine trees."
Source: CSS 2025 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2025 · Pair: Sere / Seer — Which meaning fits “Sere”?

options.A: The raised stone edge between the pavement and the road (British spelling)
options.B: Dry and withered (of plants or land)
options.C: A person who can foresee the future

questions.explanation:
Sere: Dry and withered (of plants or land). Sentence: "By June the fields were sere and brown after months without rain."
Seer: A person believed to be able to see the future; a prophet. Sentence: "The villagers asked the old seer to predict whether the coming year would bring rain."
Source: CSS 2025 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2025 · Pair: Crepuscular / Crepitation — Which meaning fits “Crepuscular”?

options.A: Relating to twilight; (of animals) active at dawn and dusk
options.B: An insulting or mocking remark; to taunt
options.D: A person believed to be able to see the future; a prophet

questions.explanation:
Crepuscular: Relating to twilight; (of animals) active at dawn and dusk. Sentence: "Deer are crepuscular animals, coming out to graze in the dim light at dawn and dusk."
Crepitation: A crackling or rattling sound, e.g. of fire, broken bones or the lungs. Sentence: "The doctor heard crepitation in the patient's lungs, a crackling sign of pneumonia."
Source: CSS 2025 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2025 · Pair: Uxoricide / Uxorious — Which meaning fits “Uxoricide”?

options.A: Excessively fond of or submissive to one's wife
options.B: A joke or playful remark; to speak in fun
options.C: Rich and profuse in growth; lush
options.D: The killing of a wife by her husband

questions.explanation:
Uxoricide: The killing of a wife by her husband. Sentence: "He was convicted of uxoricide after investigators proved he had murdered his wife."
Uxorious: Excessively fond of or submissive to one's wife. Sentence: "He was so uxorious that he could not decide even what to eat without asking his wife."
Source: CSS 2025 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).
